text:
Maya: Thanks again for joining the all-hands Q&A. Quick follow-up thread — capture top asks and why we won/lost deals. Please drop short notes + suggested owners.

Ben: Short note from sales — lost a midmarket deal yesterday. Primary blocker = SSO + audit logs + customer-managed KMS. They said price was fine but couldn't sign without KMS/VPC isolation.

Nora: Win example — startup embedded us because Dedicated gave predictable latency during bursts. They called out token-level billing clarity and the per-route tracing as reasons to choose us.

Claire: From product side: can folks confirm which of these are roadmap items vs supportable workarounds? Need to align messaging to sales ASAP.

Rishi: Timeline check: Hosted KMS (integrated) targeted Q3 '26. Dedicated/Private KMS & on-prem HSM options targeted Q4 '26. VPC peering / private networking alpha for select customers in Q3 '26. Prioritization driven by ARR signal / open contracts.

Ben: Request: can we get a concise sales one-pager listing compliance/capability status + ETA and suggested fallback talking points for when feature isn't GA?

Maya: Good ask. Claire — can you own the one-pager?

Claire: Yes, will put together a sales-ready deck + one-pager. Also we need an engineering runbook for explaining quantization/latency tradeoffs to customers — who can help with that?

Jules: I can draft the quantization runbook. I'll include a small perf vs cost table (7B int8 vs 13B int8/4-bit) and examples of KV cache impact on latency.

Sam: Another recurring ask from prospects: explicit per-route latency SLOs surfaced in the Console. Right now we have autoscaling + burst policies, but customers want per-route percentiles and a way to pin SLOs.

Rishi: Short-term we can surface per-route latency percentiles and historical charts in Console (target mid-Q3). Long-term we should expose SLO enforcement via smart routing and fallback policies (end of year roadmap).

Nora: Customers also want a reproducible demo harness — a sandbox that runs representative traffic and shows the config used to generate published perf numbers. They flagged certificate/tenant setup as painful.

Maya: Action item: collect clear examples of wins where canary rollouts / fallback policies prevented outages or regressions, and losses where missing features were the decisive factor. We'll feed those into product prioritization.

Ben: Another loss datapoint — model quality drift concern. Buyer requested continual eval hooks and regression alerts. Is Eval-as-a-Service on the horizon?

Claire: Redwood Optimize roadmap already includes evaluation monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets in Q4 '26. For now, solutions engineering can run manual evals — we should make that more accessible as a stopgap.

Maya: Please add owners to each action so I can consolidate tomorrow.

OpsBot: New doc created: https://internal.redwood/corp/all-hands/customer-retro-1948001234 — add notes and links there.

Jules: Proposed owners + schedule:
- Quantization runbook: Jules, draft by Tue
- Per-route percentiles mock UI: Sam, prototype by Fri
- Sales one-pager + deck: Claire, draft by next Wed
- Loss reasons compilation: Ben, list by EOW
- Customer quotes & links: Nora, collect by next Tue

Rishi: I'll escalate KMS / VPC peering prioritization in exec review next week. If we see >3 deals blocked by the same thing, we bump it.

Maya: Thanks all — if you have quick additions drop them here. I'll consolidate into the doc and ping owners tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:

Ben: adding a note — include suggested short-term mitigations (e.g., SOC2 evidence pack, temporary SE-managed KMS proof-of-concept) so sales can keep deals moving.

Claire: Agreed. I'll add a 'temporary mitigations' slide in the deck.

Nora: I'll also attach anonymized customer quotes that explicitly say why they left/chose us.

Maya: Perfect. Closing this thread for now, but feel free to keep appending. I'll post the consolidated action checklist later.

OpsBot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up sync (owners) in 3 days — calendar invite will be sent.
